items.title: Google Deepmind's "Humanity's First Exam" shows top AI models still fail simple everyday tasks under repeated runs
items.summary: Google Deepmind tests the reliability of 18 AI models with "Humanity's First Exam." Top models solve nearly every task family at least once, but even leaders like OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra stumble when asked for 16 straight correct answers. Visual perception accounts for 73 percent of errors, and more compute time doesn't fix the problem. items.title: Robotics startup Embo raises $110 million in seed funding to build world-model AI for robots
items.summary: Embo raised $110 million in seed funding to build a universal robot brain with world models. Its AI learns how the physical world works from internet video and practices motor skills in simulation. Google Deepmind, Meta, and MIT researchers are behind the startup as the race for general-purpose robotics AI accelerates. items.title: OpenAI countersues Apple over trade secret theft and alleged coercion of shared suppliers
items.summary: OpenAI is suing Apple in a California court, accusing it of trade secret theft and of coercing shared suppliers. The countersuit follows Apple's own lawsuit from the summer. Just two years ago, the two companies teamed up to bring ChatGPT to the iPhone. Now OpenAI is building its own devices to compete directly with Apple. items.title: Banned Nvidia Blackwell chips turn up in a Shanghai data center linked to Alice Huang, Bloomberg reports
items.summary: Two Chinese companies installed Nvidia's powerful Blackwell chips at a Shanghai data center linked to Alice Huang, according to a Bloomberg investigation. A serial number led Bloomberg to Taiwanese manufacturer Gigabyte. Exporting these chips to China without a US license is illegal. items.title: Three studies from Meta and AMI Labs back Yann LeCun's bet on JEPA world models over large language models
items.summary: Yann LeCun is pushing forward with his alternative to language models through his startup AMI Labs. The JEPA architecture aims to give machines an internal world model that captures cause and effect. Three new studies show progress in robot planning, more efficient training, and error correction, though the pieces still need to grow together. items.title: OpenAI is building "Athena" data platform to cut down on AI agent guesswork
items.summary: OpenAI's data agent in ChatGPT Work still isn't accurate enough. Under the codename "Athena," the company is building a semantic layer that gives agents standardized definitions for business metrics. The tool could also put OpenAI in direct competition with Snowflake and Databricks. The article OpenAI is building "Athena" data platform to cut down on AI agent guesswork appeared first on The Decoder.

items.title: Rockstar's AI dilemma: Can GTA 6's staggered release model survive coding agents?
items.summary: More than 40 projects are working to bring a leaked Xbox build of GTA 6 to PC through reverse engineering just days after its $3.79 billion record console launch. AI coding agents like Claude Code are speeding up the process so much that an early unofficial multiplayer mode is already running. Rockstar's delayed PC business model is coming under pressure. items.title: Former OpenAI researcher says the Riemann proof matters less than the fact that an AI system can produce it
items.summary: Complexity theorist and former OpenAI researcher Scott Aaronson argues that AI's recent math breakthroughs matter far beyond academia. The possible consequences, he writes, range from reshaping the global economy to threatening all life on Earth. He's also "virtually certain" that AI labs are sitting on "one or more bombshells" in cryptography.
